leverage.exposure: A leveraged position is open and has been through several runs. It costs nothing until the instant the matchday locks, at which point a negative balance scores zero for the entire matchday, so this is a deadline risk rather than a running one. The lock is still comfortably far off, which is why this is not an emergency, but the sale that clears it has now been outstanding long enough to be worth saying plainly. Sequencing is flexible: the flip can be bought before the sale without breaching the floor, and the squad never dips below eleven along any ordering of the sale, the bench buy, the flip and its unwind. The one hard constraint is that the flip must be sold back after the next daily tick and before the lock, and that the balance must be non-negative at that moment.

binding_gap: The gap is defensive, and it is not fixable this cycle. After the sale the back four has no alternative and its fourth member is a minimum-priced body. An upgrade there would have to be funded outright rather than merely unwound, because a player kept through the lock is paid for permanently, and the cushion left after the sale and the bench buy is a rounding error next to any defender worth starting. This is the same conclusion the ledger reached when the obvious upgrade target was lost at auction earlier today, and nothing since has changed it. The gap closes when the balance is healthy, not before.

verdict.detail: The balance is still negative and Treu is still in the squad, so the one action that decides whether MD5 scores at all has not been taken. Everything else on this page is secondary to that. There is no new reason to delay: the case for holding Treu to capture another tick was examined and rejected two runs ago, and the realised tick came in at a third of the signal, which makes the delay worth even less than the estimate that was already judged too small to matter. Sell him back to Kickbase, which pays exactly market value with no spread, and the deficit clears with room to spare.

sell.reason: One sale, already standing, and it is unconditional as to whether and free only as to when: Treu, by instant sale back to Kickbase. He is fit and starting, so this is not an availability call — it is the funding leg of a leveraged position, and his relatively weak scoring average makes him the right player to lose from a squad that has to shed someone. Nothing else should be sold. Any second sale drops the squad below a fillable formation, and there is no replacement that could land first.

COST OF THE SALE, STATED PLAINLY: Nakuzola (ap 27) replaces him in the XI, so the sale costs roughly 49 points of expected average, and it leaves ZERO bench — see the companion BUY on Bachmann, which is the insurance against that.

buy.reason: No points buy is affordable and none should be attempted. Anything kept through the lock has to be paid for outright, and what remains after the sale buys a body and nothing more. The one purchase worth making is exactly that body: a minimum-priced midfielder as bench insurance, so that a single late absence in the forced eleven does not trigger the under-eleven penalty. He is not a tick candidate and was correctly rejected as one; this buys him as cover, where the trend flag is irrelevant. Every other listing on the board was swept and rejected, the newest on two independent grounds — a falling trend flag and a live status flag.

movers.reason: The flip the last run recommended was lost, and losing it was the right outcome rather than a failure. It cleared to the league's most active trader at a premium well above the entire measured downside of the trend-flag edge, so winning it at that price would have been an expected loss. That is the clearest vindication the bid-at-market-value-and-never-raise rule has had: the discipline is what stopped this run paying a contested price for a coin flip. The replacement is the backup keeper at the head of the reserve queue, bid at exactly market value, with the Leipzig teenager as the fallback if that one is lost too. Only one of them can be run, not both — the bench buy eats enough of the cushion to put the pair outside the sizing rule, and in any case the capital cannot be recycled between their two expiry times because a won flip stays locked until the next daily tick. Expect to lose the auction. Roughly half of board purchases clear at or below market value, and on the contested half a market-value bid simply loses, at no cost. The edge itself was re-measured from the refreshed log and shows no decay at all — the rising-trend flag is performing slightly better than the figure the task prompt carries, on nearly double the sample. The two open questions stand unresolved: whether the game caps squad size, which would cap how many flips can be run at once, and the fact that this edge is measured in one league over one period and will erode if rivals crowd in. On present evidence they have not crowded it out, though they are plainly working the same mechanism — several of them dumped a large block of players back to the market within an hour of the last tick.

fitness.sweep: Nothing to flag. No squad player is newly injured, suspended or benched, and none appears on the current injured-and-suspended table. The web leg succeeded this run and the table dated itself cleanly through its relative absence durations and a same-day entry, so the undated-page trap that broke an earlier run did not bite. Worth carrying forward: the game's own status flag and the public injury table disagree at the margin — the newest listing carried a live status flag while not appearing on the table at all — and the status flag is the faster of the two. Trust it when they conflict.
